record.field: Build dashboards the user can open in Odoo. You describe what to show — models, filters, groupings and measures — and Odoo draws and stores it. You never write code, SQL or markup, and a saved dashboard holds the question rather than the numbers, so it is recalculated with the permissions of whoever opens it.

Return the dashboard specification format: the widget types, the aggregates and date granularities available, the layout grid, the limits, and a complete worked example. Call this before building your first dashboard in a conversation — it is short, and a spec written without it is usually refused for a fixable reason.
List the saved dashboards this user can open, with their ids, owners and a one-line description of each. Use it to find the id of a dashboard the user refers to by name.

Return one dashboard's full specification. Always call this before changing an existing dashboard: edit the spec you get back and save that, rather than rebuilding from scratch, so the parts the user was happy with stay exactly as they were.

For a given model, return the numeric fields worth totalling and the fields worth grouping by. A quick way to propose a sensible dashboard for a model you have not worked with before, without reading the whole schema.

Validate a specification, save it as a preview, and return a link plus a sample of the real figures each tile produces. Prefer this over save_dashboard when building something new: the preview does not appear on the user's app tile, and the sample lets you check the numbers look sensible before asking them to look. If a figure seems wrong, say so and fix the spec rather than presenting it.

{"type": "object", "properties": {"spec": {"type": "object", "description": "The dashboard specification. Call get_dashboard_schema for the format."}, "name": {"type": "string", "description": "Optional. Defaults to the spec's title."}}, "required": ["spec"], "additionalProperties": false}

Save a dashboard so it appears on the user's AI Dashboards app tile. Pass a dashboard_id to update an existing one (publishing a preview, or applying a change), or a spec alone to create and save in one step. Only the owner can change a dashboard; for someone else's, suggest they duplicate it. Every save keeps the previous version, so a change can always be undone.

Delete a dashboard permanently. Only its owner can. Confirm with the user first — the dashboard and its whole history go, and this cannot be undone.

When the user asks for a dashboard, report, chart or KPI in Odoo, build it with the dashboard tools rather than answering with a table in chat — they get something they can open again tomorrow. Call get_dashboard_schema first, then get_schema on each model you intend to use so the field names are real rather than guessed. Prefer preview_dashboard over save_dashboard for anything new, check the sample figures it returns, and only then invite the user to look. To change an existing dashboard, read it with get_dashboard and edit that specification.
